business_problem: KION's service technicians write maintenance reports for industrial trucks under time pressure, so the reports often contain abbreviations and colloquial wording that make them hard to read, translate, correct, and consistently classify into recurring fault categories.
solution_summary: KION Group built MERLIN as a productively used generative AI tool for maintenance and quality workflows around its industrial trucks. Service reports created after maintenance appointments are stored and processed on the KION Analytics Platform (KAP), whose cloud resources are used to store data and train the machine learning model. In the first phase, MERLIN uses a glossary plus contextual signals such as the truck model, series, and spare part references mentioned in each report to expand KION-specific abbreviations, correct spelling issues, and translate the documentation into English, creating a consistent dataset for downstream analysis. On top of that normalized data, a custom-built classification model searches for patterns and assigns reports to recurring "master problems." Results are uploaded as confidence-scored proposals for manual review, while the wider data lake and Dremio query layer let teams consolidate and pull data from multiple internal sources.

MERLIN uses a glossary plus truck model, series, and spare-part context to correct and translate the text into English, then a classification model detects patterns and maps reports to master problems. business_outcome: KION reduced the time and cost of translating and classifying maintenance reports, removed dependence on an external translation agency, enabled more frequent report availability, and freed quality teams to focus more on solving customer problems and making recommendations.
